findings.evidence: W-1's core guard `if Path(toplevel) != ctx.home.resolve(): return FAIL, f"git toplevel {toplevel} is not the control home"` is never exercised: the only W-1 defect test (`test_w1_fail_in_repo`, defect `not-git-root`) moves `.git` into `nested/` so `rev-parse` fails outright and the FIRST branch fires ("not inside a git repo"); deleting the toplevel comparison leaves every test in the package green.
findings.required_change: Add a FAIL-path test where `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeds but returns a directory other than the home (e.g. home is a plain subdirectory of an initialized repo), asserting the `git toplevel ... is not the control home` detail — removing the comparison must make that test fail.

findings.evidence: The module Laws claim "malformed input never produces a raw traceback", but check_c12 does `secrets.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` and `gitignore.read_text(...)` with no UnicodeDecodeError handling; run_verify catches only `(EngineError, FP.FixtureError)` and `OSError`, and UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError subclass — a non-UTF-8 factory/SECRETS.md or .gitignore escapes as a raw traceback, no PREFLIGHT.md is written, and the asserted fail-closed invariant is not delivered. parse_toml, check_a7 and check_a8 all catch UnicodeDecodeError; check_c12 does not, and no test feeds a non-UTF-8 file to it.
findings.required_change: Handle UnicodeDecodeError in check_c12's two read_text calls with a named FAIL detail (as parse_toml does), or widen run_verify's named-error catch to cover it, and add a defect test (non-UTF-8 SECRETS.md) asserting a named FAIL row and no traceback.

findings.evidence: missing_protections validates parameters only for `pull_request` (`required_approving_review_count >= 1`); for `required_status_checks` it checks type presence only. A ruleset carrying a `required_status_checks` rule with an empty or absent checks parameter passes C-3/W-7 while the PASS detail claims full protection — the guard is defeated by a widened input. Every ruleset test removes or adds rule TYPES (`test_c3_fail_empty_rules`, `test_c3_fail_single_missing_protection`); none exercises a present-but-empty required_status_checks parameter.
findings.required_change: Either validate that the `required_status_checks` rule carries a non-empty checks parameter in missing_protections, or state explicitly in the check detail that only type presence is claimed; add a ruleset-dataset test with an empty required_status_checks parameter pinning the chosen semantics.

findings.evidence: In run_attest the malformed-scoped-id guard (`if check_id.count(":") != 1 or not binding.strip()`) is nested inside `if binding:`, so it is unreachable for the empty-binding case: `attest <home> C-13: --by x --note y` partitions to binding="", skips the block, and appends a row for the meaningless id "C-13:" to the append-only ledger instead of the named refusal `unknown check id`; no test covers a trailing-colon id.
findings.required_change: Reject a check_id containing ":" with an empty or whitespace-only binding before the declared-binding lookup (named EngineError, rc 1), and add a CLI test asserting the refusal message and a byte-identical ledger.

findings.evidence: load_registry hard-requires a bool `required` per check row, but the gate computation `green = summary["failed"] == 0` never consults it — every FAIL gates regardless of the flag, and the flag drives no output. A production registry change flipping a CORE check to `required: false` leaves behavior and output byte-identical: the validated field is nominal, and no test pins what `required` means for gating.
findings.required_change: Either gate on `required` (only required FAILs force RED, non-required FAILs render as named non-gating rows) with a test that flips a check's flag and observes the rc change, or drop the misleading per-row bool from the registry schema and its validation.

findings.evidence: append_attest builds `event_id = f"onboard-attest-{check_id}-{int(time.time())}"` and dedupes against a ledger snapshot loaded before the append (TOCTOU): two concurrent attest runs within the same unix second both load the same `existing` set, both conclude the id is free, and both append — duplicate event_ids hit the ledger's uniqueness law, and on LedgerError the dedupe silently degrades to `existing = set()` (no collision check at all).
findings.required_change: Make the append collision-safe under concurrent runs (e.g. re-read/verify uniqueness inside the append path or derive a suffix from content the snapshot cannot collide on) and add an operational test appending two attests for the same check within one second asserting distinct event_ids and a valid ledger.

findings.evidence: test_read_only_hash_walk computes `changed = {k for k in after if k not in before or before.get(k) != after[k]}` and `added = set(after) - set(before)` — both keyed on `after`, so files DELETED by a verify run never appear; a production change making verify unlink any home file outside the sanctioned set keeps the read-only-law test green.
findings.required_change: Include deletions in the walk comparison (`set(before) - set(after)` must also be a subset of the sanctioned set, or empty) so removing the guard fails the test.

findings.evidence: home_states() wraps the installed state_machine import/exec in `except Exception: pass` and silently falls back to the kit's SM.STATES; W-8's comparison baseline therefore changes without any signal in the detail line ("Stage options cover all N pipeline states" names neither authority nor N's source). A production change that makes the installed module raise (or a truncated STATES list in it) silently swaps or shrinks the authority W-8 checks against; no test covers a broken or divergent installed state_machine.py.
findings.required_change: Name the authority used in the W-8 detail (installed vs kit fallback), and add a test with a broken/short-STATES installed factory/tools/state_machine.py pinning the fallback behavior and the detail wording.

findings.evidence: env_ref_problems silently skips non-string refs (`if not isinstance(ref, str) or CV.is_deferred(ref): continue`) and resolves `file:` refs as `(ctx.home / ref[5:]).exists()` — an absolute or `../`-escaping path resolves outside the home, so a production change declaring `refs = ["file:/etc/passwd"]` or a dict-valued ref passes W-3's presence guard without any credential material under the home. No test covers a non-string ref or a home-escaping file: ref.
findings.required_change: Refuse (named W-3 problem) non-string refs and file: refs that resolve outside the home, and add tests for both escapes.

findings.evidence: applicability's `control_home not declared (workspace.toml unreadable or invalid)` N-A branch (mode "unknown") turns off ALL eight mode:dedicated checks, and N-A never gates; apply_defects has no defect that removes or garbles the `control_home` key while keeping the TOML parseable, so no test shows whether a valid workspace.toml that merely omits control_home still forces RED via C-10 or silently greens with W-1..W-8 all N-A.
findings.required_change: Add a defect test (workspace.toml without `control_home`, otherwise valid) pinning the intended outcome: either a named FAIL from an always-applicable check or the N-A rendering with its rc, so widening applicability to unknown-mode cannot silently disable the WORKSPACE category.

findings.required_change: Either delete the unused hash_walk helper from onboarding/readiness.py or make the hash-walk tests (test_read_only_hash_walk, test_fixture_trees_pristine) call it; in both cases the docstring must stop claiming usage that does not exist.

findings.evidence: Contract acceptance: "The test-out scripts ship and run green against `benchmark-app` as a smoke." The Diff stat ships only 4 files (onboarding/readiness.py, onboarding/registry.json, onboarding/tests/test_readiness.py, onboarding/tests/test_docs_consistency.py) — no hunk ships a test-out script or touches benchmark-app — and the gate evidence records only `python3 -m unittest`, `python3 tools/gates/test_gate.py`, `python3 tools/config_validator.py templates/...`, and CI runs at head; no benchmark-app smoke run appears anywhere in the package. The closest acceptance artifact in the Diff is the fixture-scoped bad-home run ("The acceptance run of record: every seeded defect FAILs precisely."), which does not cover this criterion.
findings.required_change: Show acceptance criterion 3 satisfied inside the review record: add gate evidence of the shipped test-out scripts running green against benchmark-app as a smoke at head 2bd431c, or ship/point to the test-out script hunks this slice adds, or record an explicit owner-approved deviation deferring the benchmark-app smoke (as the contract already does only for the FULL conformance smoke, not for the test-out script smoke).

findings.evidence: Module docstring claims "Every required check also has a FAIL-path test via the make_home/verify_home generator (one defect per test, precise detail assertions)." — but the package shows no FAIL-path test for the required checks C-9 and W-5: "C-9" appears only in the good-home PASS list (test_readiness.py:226) and the registry-id enumeration (test_readiness.py:1374), and no defect in apply_defects or dataset mutation exercises W-5 (test_c8_fail_ledger_invalid asserts C-8 only); the claimed coverage has no corresponding artifact for these two checks.
findings.required_change: Add FAIL-path tests for C-9 (e.g. toolchain probe failure) and W-5 (e.g. ledger-invalid asserted on the W-5 row), or correct the module docstring so the coverage claim matches the tests actually shipped.

findings.evidence: Module docstring states "ONE test asserting:" followed by the pipeline/deleted-asset assertions, but the same file ships TWO test methods: "+    def test_kickoff_template_gate_list_includes_spec_freeze(self):" (test_docs_consistency.py:60) and "+    def test_docs_name_the_pipeline_and_drop_deleted_assets(self) -> None:" (test_docs_consistency.py:77) — the docstring does not describe the shipped contents.
findings.required_change: Update the module docstring of onboarding/tests/test_docs_consistency.py to describe both shipped tests (the G7 KICKOFF-template gate-list test and the pipeline/deleted-asset test).

findings.evidence: run_verify: `if forge_fixture: forge = FP.Forge.from_fixture(forge_fixture)` — the --forge-fixture flag swaps the gh transport for a dataset-backed one, and nothing records that the run was fixture-backed: PREFLIGHT.md and the --json payload (`"status": "GREEN" if green else "RED"`) are byte-shaped identically to a live-probe run.
findings.required_change: Make fixture-backed runs distinguishable at every output surface: record the forge transport mode (live vs fixture file path) in PREFLIGHT.md and in the --json payload, or refuse --forge-fixture outside a test environment, so a fabricated-dataset GREEN can never masquerade as live gate evidence.

findings.evidence: applicability: `if applies == "mode:dedicated": if ctx.control_home == "dedicated": return None; if ctx.control_home == "in-repo": return ...; return "control_home not declared (workspace.toml unreadable or invalid)"` — Context sets `self.control_home = ch if isinstance(ch, str) else None` with no enum validation, so a declared but unrecognized value (control_home = "garbage") renders ALL W-1..W-8 checks N-A and skips check_c13's binding-scoped attest requirement (`if ctx.control_home != "dedicated" ...: return status, detail`), with no FAIL raised at readiness.py's own boundary; no test covers a non-enum control_home value.
findings.required_change: Validate control_home against the closed enum {dedicated, in-repo} when it is present: a declared but unrecognized value must produce a named FAIL (fail closed), not N-A scope reduction of the dedicated-mode checks and the C-13 binding attest requirement.

findings.evidence: check_c12: `if not secrets.is_file() or not secrets.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()` and `text = gitignore.read_text(encoding="utf-8").lower()` read target-controlled bytes with no UnicodeDecodeError handling; run_verify only catches `(EngineError, FP.FixtureError)` and `OSError`, so a non-UTF-8 SECRETS.md or .gitignore raises a raw traceback that kills the whole verify — no named FAIL row, no PREFLIGHT.md, no summary — contradicting the module's own law "malformed input never produces a raw traceback"; the FAIL-path tests ("no-secrets-doc", "bad-gitignore") only use valid UTF-8, so they stay green regardless of decode handling.
findings.required_change: Guard every target-file read in the check implementations (C-12 in particular) for UnicodeDecodeError and convert it to a named FAIL detail for that check, so one malformed file yields a precise FAIL instead of aborting the entire verify with a traceback; add a non-UTF-8 fixture test.

findings.evidence: env_ref_problems: `elif ref.startswith("file:"): if not (ctx.home / ref[5:]).exists()` — the file: credential ref is joined onto the home with no confinement: an absolute path (`ctx.home / "/etc/passwd"` resolves to `/etc/passwd` under pathlib) or a ../ traversal escapes the control home, and W-3 then PASSes on a credential that lives outside the workspace while the FAIL detail doubles as an existence oracle for arbitrary paths.
findings.required_change: Resolve file: refs against ctx.home and require the resolved path to stay within the home (reject absolute paths and ..-escapes with a named problem) before the existence check.

findings.evidence: home_states: `spec.loader.exec_module(mod)` is wrapped in `except Exception: pass  # fall through to the kit authority` — a broken or hostile installed factory/tools/state_machine.py that raises during import is silently discarded with no named detail anywhere, and W-8 then validates the board against the kit's STATES without the output ever revealing that the home's declared authority failed to load.
findings.required_change: Narrow the catch and surface the failure: record a named detail (in the W-8 row or an advisory) when the installed state_machine exists but fails to import, so the silent fallback to the kit authority is visible in verify output.

findings.evidence: append_attest validates only `if not isinstance(by, str) or not by.strip()` and find_attest accepts any row where `isinstance(by, str) and by.strip()` — the human-gate identity is a fully self-declared arbitrary string; rows carrying decision "approved" are written and trusted with no binding to any authenticated identity (the forge's auth login is already probed by C-2 via `ctx.forge.auth_scopes()`), so any actor able to run the CLI mints an approved human_gate PASS for C-13/U-*/A-* under any name.
findings.required_change: Bind the attest identity to an authenticated source: cross-check --by against the forge's authenticated login (or record the authenticated login alongside the claimed one in the row) so a human-gate PASS carries verifiable attribution.

findings.evidence: write_preflight: `detail = (r.get("detail") or "").replace("|", "\\|")` escapes pipes but not newlines, and details can embed ledger-controlled strings (attest_status renders `attested by {row.get('answered_by')}`); a crafted answered_by (or subprocess error text) containing a newline injects forged rows (e.g. a fake `| C-3 | CORE | PASS | ... |` line) into the regenerated PREFLIGHT.md report.
findings.required_change: Sanitize detail strings before table interpolation — strip or escape CR/LF and collapse each detail to a single line in write_preflight — so report rows can never be injected from ledger or subprocess content.
